change.title: pr-4
change.description: FEATURE: Embeddable Discourse comments, now with simple-rss instead of feedzirra
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Embed URL goes unescaped into a raw-HTML post, so an anonymous visitor can store XSS
findings.body: `url` is interpolated straight into `#{url}`, and the post is saved with `cook_method: raw_html` (line 22). `Post#cook` then returns `raw` without sanitizing it (app/models/post.rb:133). For `import_remote`, `url` is the visitor-supplied `embed_url` from `/embed/best` (embed_controller.rb:9,15 → retrieve_topic.rb:17 → topic_retriever.rb:52). The only checks are that the host equals `embeddable_host` (topic_retriever.rb:15) and that the Referer host matches, and a non-browser client can forge the Referer. A URL such as `http:///?a='onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)'` gets past `URI()`, and most blogs answer a query-string URL with a 200. The resulting topic, posted as `embed_by_username`, carries attacker-controlled attributes that render unescaped on the forum and in the embed (best.html.erb:19). The `^` anchor on line 11 matches at the start of any line, not only the start of the string, so it does not limit this either. Fix: HTML-escape `url` (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`), anchor with `\A`, and sanitize raw_html content before storing it.

findings.title: Anonymous visitors can create unlimited topics by varying the embed_url
findings.body: The throttle key is the full `@embed_url`, so each distinct query string or fragment on the embeddable host counts as a new URL. Each one is fetched, then imported as a new topic (topic_embed.rb:20-30) owned by `embed_by_username`. Nothing requires the requester to be logged in: embed_controller.rb:15 passes `current_user.try(:id)`, which is nil for anonymous visitors. A script looping over `?n=1..N` with a forged Referer fills the forum with duplicate topics. Normalize the URL (drop the query and fragment, or require it to appear in the feed) and add a throttle that is not keyed per URL.

findings.title: Remote fetches have no overall timeout, and the loading page reloads forever
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` here and `open(url).read` in topic_embed.rb:48 are open-uri calls with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, so how long they can block is whatever Net::HTTP's defaults allow. TopicRetriever runs the whole feed poll synchronously (topic_retriever.rb:41) and then the HTTP fetch, so one retrieve job can block a Sidekiq worker for the sum of both waits. When retrieval fails (404, timeout, feed error), loading.html.erb reloads every 30s with no limit and enqueues another job each time, and the reader never sees an error. Pass explicit timeouts to `open` and stop the reload after a few attempts.

findings.title: `i.content` is nil for plain RSS 2.0 items, so one such item aborts the whole poll
findings.body: In SimpleRSS, `content` comes from Atom `<content>` or `content:encoded`. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only supply `<description>`, and for those `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Nothing rescues the error, so the hourly job (retry: false) fails and imports nothing, and every retrieve job that runs it (topic_retriever.rb:41) fails too. Fall back to `i.description`, and rescue errors per item so one bad item doesn't block the rest.

findings.title: The Disqus import no longer keeps thread dates or supports `--category`
findings.body: The earlier code passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and `category:`. `import_remote` accepts only `title`, so imported topics now get today's date, and the `-c` option is gone. Each thread also now triggers a live HTTP fetch of `t[:link]`, and any fetch error (e.g. a 404) aborts the whole import.

findings.title: The postMessage origin check is a substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl. With `http://forum.example.com/`, a message from `http://forum.example.co` passes. Today the only effect is a resized iframe, but compare against the exact origin, e.g. `e.origin === discourseUrl.replace(/\/$/, '')`.

findings.title: `force: true` added to a migration that has already shipped
findings.body: Instances that have already run this migration will not run it again, so the edit has no effect there. Where it does run, `force: true` silently drops an existing `top_topics` table. `create_topic_embeds` uses `force: true` too, without a reason. Remove both.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` makes the next line the `if` condition
findings.body: `end if` is a modifier `if`, and its condition is whatever expression ERB emits next (the output of the logo link). The view only renders because that append happens to be truthy. Replace it with `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: The 404 test fails for a different reason than its name says
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` runs before `params.require`, and with `embeddable_host` blank by default it raises InvalidAccess (403). The test therefore never reaches the missing-`embed_url` path, and `should_not be_success` hides the difference. Stub a valid host and Referer, and assert the specific status.

findings.title: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string
findings.body: `import` appends the footer to the argument in place, so the caller's string changes, and a frozen string literal would raise. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

contracts.action: Anonymous GET /embed/best with an unknown embed_url enqueues retrieve_topic
contracts.before_after: The host must equal embeddable_host. The per-URL redis setnx throttle lasts 60s and is skipped for staff. If the URL is not yet known, PollFeed runs, then the HTTP fetch, then import as embed_by_username.
contracts.visible_effect: The loading page reloads every 30s until a topic exists. A forged URL creates a topic containing unescaped HTML.
contracts.failure_mode: Fetch errors are not caught and the job fails without notice. The loading page keeps reloading forever.

contracts.action: What bounds the whole retrieval wait
contracts.before_after: The feed poll runs synchronously, then the HTTP fetch runs. Neither has an explicit timeout.
contracts.failure_mode: Only Net::HTTP's defaults bound the wait, and the sequential waits add up. Nothing caps the whole operation.

contracts.action: Embed responses are put in the anonymous cache
contracts.before_after: Caches for 1 minute when can_cache_content? is true.
contracts.visible_effect: The cached loading page or topic HTML is served to other anonymous embedders.
contracts.failure_mode: A cache hit may skip ensure_embeddable and serve a response that embeds another visitor's Referer. Not verified.
contracts.open_question: Does AnonymousCache key on the Referer, and does it serve hits before the controller filters run?

summary: Adds embeddable comments, RSS/remote import, and posts stored as raw HTML. Blocker: the visitor-supplied embed_url is put unescaped into a post that is rendered as raw HTML, so an anonymous visitor with a forged Referer can store XSS. The same path lets anyone create unlimited topics by varying the URL. Also: remote fetches have no overall timeout and the loading page reloads forever; the feed poll crashes on RSS items without `content`; the Disqus import lost thread dates and `--category`.
